recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-25038 unless FHIR-I later wants a broader editorial restatement of the existing SHOULD wording.
issue_request: FHIR-25038 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I clarification for the FHIR-core HTTP update interaction. It asked that update success wording stop implying a SHALL requirement for ETag, and the approved resolution also clarified that Last-Modified was not intended to be SHALL; where the server supports FHIR versioning, the headers should be SHOULD-level guidance.
initial_application: No explicit source commit mentioning FHIR-25038 was found. The current application appears to have occurred implicitly in c32a2adb0774d63553808f9e2b551292292e7fed, a 2022-05-11 HTTP update response change for FHIR-26358 that split the old SHALL sentence and replaced the ETag/Last-Modified requirement with separate SHOULD wording. Jira was then updated on 2022-05-16 to say build.fhir.org/http.html#update already showed the requested update.
additional_context: publish.ini maps http.html to the built HTTP page, so source/http.html is in current build scope. FHIR-I minutes from 2020-03-23 confirm the FHIR-25038 decision, including that this was a clarification to poorly written normative wording. Later FHIR-39117 addressed the same optionality principle in the HTTP interaction summary table by changing ETag/Last-Modified from required to optional, and that issue is already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-26358, whose source commit carried the effective wording change, is also already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: An empty audit commit was published. The current update interaction text says successful update/create responses SHALL use the correct 200/201 status and SHALL return Location, but separately says servers SHOULD return an ETag with versionId when versioning is supported and a Last-Modified header. This preserves the Jira-approved clarification that ETag and Last-Modified are not mandatory update response headers.

related_jiras.note: Its HTTP update response commit separated the mandatory Location requirement from the optional ETag/Last-Modified guidance, effectively applying FHIR-25038 while addressing conditional create/update Location handling.
It later aligned the HTTP response summary table with the same optional ETag/Last-Modified principle and is already audited on the combined branch.

A later HTTP create-operation guidance issue surfaced in bounded Jira search because it also mentions response Location, Last-Modified, and ETag behavior; it is separate from the update-response optionality decision.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I clarification that update responses should not imply mandatory ETag or Last-Modified headers.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the target behavior: successful update response headers are SHOULD-level when versioning is supported, not a SHALL requirement.

evidence_items.summary: FHIR-I minutes record FHIR-25038 as accepted Persuasive with Modification by 6-0-0 and note it is a normative clarification of poorly written original wording.
evidence_items.learned: The work-group meeting record confirms the Jira decision and supports treating the current optionality wording as a clarification, not a new mandatory requirement.

evidence_items.summary: publish.ini maps http.html to the built HTTP page, and the current update section separates mandatory status/Location behavior from SHOULD-level ETag and Last-Modified guidance.
evidence_items.learned: The build-scoped current source already applies the requested optional ETag and Last-Modified semantics.

evidence_items.summary: The 2022-05-11 FHIR-26358 HTTP commit removed the old update sentence requiring Last-Modified and ETag and added a separate SHOULD sentence for those headers.
evidence_items.learned: This identifies the implicit application path for FHIR-25038 even though no FHIR-25038-tagged source commit was found.
